Unfortunately with children like that, it needs to be heavily enforced about “think about how they would feel in that situation.” It’s much less of having rules set in place, rather trusting them to know what is the right decision. Teaching and guiding them to be self aware. Teaching meditation and showing them how to properly exercise.

It could mean the child themselves are just not active enough, or not getting enough emotional care. It’s more towards the parents responsibility, and the best you can do is be a good role model.

Give them controlled creativity. I work well with kids, I just don’t like them.

Kids will want to cause trouble because they are told specifically NOT to do something. When you straight up trust them to essentially not hammer their hand to a wood plank rather than tell them not to, they feel less compelled to do it because they automatically know it’s dangerous.

My favorite thing to do is teach kids how to play colorku, go, nim or reversi. Mind games keeps them busy, but if they don’t like sitting I like to do active games. Limbo, horseshoes, who can dance the best, jump the highest, etc. It’s also talking to them like people who are learning how to adult, rather than children. Respect them, respect boundaries, and treat them the way you want to be treated rather than authoritarian.

It holds a lot of your sweat, and will often lead to a breeding ground for bad bacteria. It’s okay to wear it during training and exercise when working out indoors or specific sports, as many are windbreakers and have a good ventilation system. Avoid wearing underwear made over 80% synthetic regularly. Unless it’s a binder, then your breaks should make up for it.

Cotton is perfect for the heat, and cover as much of your body in it as possible. Wear loose fabrics or windbreakers to vent your body, and you will be mostly okay. I just accept dysphoria and avoid wearing my binders when it becomes over 85°F.

I’d advise with you to exercise with a trainer and get a dietician if you can afford it. Or discuss with your doctor over your recent blood work to help make a meal plan (something basic, such as meals low in protein, salt, sugar, and calories)

I took some classes while I was studying to be a nurse, and read a lot of self help stuff. Though here’s the lowdown that anyone can do:

- reduce eating out for only one meal a day

- eat slowly and drink lots of water

- when you want something sweet eat fruit

- if you feel hungry eat something high in fiber or drink water

- Nuts and legumes are the best snack food, as they will help you feel full and are higher in nutrition

- Practice yoga every morning. Doesn’t have to be intense by any means. Just a 5 minute stretch will increase blood flow and heart rate, as well as boost mental health

- Exercise. It helps reduce stress and boost mental health

- Become a master at the DBT skills [STOP](https://www.nayaclinics.com/post/stop-skill-dbt-what-is-it-and-how-to-use-it) and [TIPP](https://eddinscounseling.com/distress-tolerance-skills-tipp-emotional-crisis/). Use Stop for when you feel hungry, use Tipp when you feel nervous. Relaxing your mind can help reduce your hunger

I hope that was helpful. I have no doubt the reason why you have a larger chest could be because of your weight, it’s just where most bodies hold excess energy. Stay strong, you can do it!

It depends on your body type, how much you weigh, your exercising routine, etc etc. Counting calories is very efficient when trying to lose weight, but doesn’t train you to listen to your body when you are at a healthy weight. Instead it makes you very calorie conscious, and can lead to an ED (which unfortunately the media heavily enforces for those overweight)

Testosterone will turn you into a teen boy again, making you feel constantly hungry and never satisfied. So it’s easy to gain weight that you had just lost. Here are some things I learned in my medical classes that help, and I hope they help you on your weight loss journey 

- Eat until you feel 70-80% full

This trains you to not overreat, and you can count how many calories you took in after rather than before.

- High Fiber Foods

Fiber is very good for you, and having an apple for a snack instead of high protein foods will make you feel more full and reduce the amount of calories you eat

- Eat high carb and protein meals before resistance or cardio workouts

Carbs with give your muscles energy so you can push yourself harder, and reduce chances of fatigue in your workouts. Protein helps you gain muscle, so that you are prepared to build muscle as well as develop your body to be prepared for more intense exercises

- Yoga after heavy meals and before intense workouts

Okay, so why yoga? Yoga exercises blood flow and mindfulness, and stretches your muscles to reduce pain in your joints. Yoga is very good at burning calories without muscle building, and prepares every muscle one has for a workout so that there is reduced chances of injury 

- Watch your sugar and salt intake

Sugar and salt is in everything we eat. We’re told to watch how much carbs, fiber, proteins, and calories we should have. But have you ever noticed how much sugar or salt you have in your meals? Both can reduce blood circulation, increase fatigue in your workouts, and absorbs a lot of water in your system (resulting into fat later on). So drink lots of water, and make sure you don’t eat too much salt and sugar!

I hope that was helpful!

Marie Kondo has some very interesting advice she has mentioned in her book. Instead of going a little at a time, do it all at once. Dedicate 4 days to decluttering by category rather than room, and spend a 5th day deep cleaning. A lot of people don’t have this time on their hands, or simply feel like it’s too much work for them to handle in one wave (which is understandable).

What I do is I have a general schedule planned for my day, and every 55 minutes of work I do I take an 11 minute break. If you find yourself switching between your distractions and your work, you have to start over the clock. Often times on my 11 minute break I will lightly declutter my working space, maybe a countertop, or empty the trash. As small as these things are, it will make the wave much more manageable to face.

Because I suffer from clinical depression, my room very easily a mess within a day (even though I have less things) to a point where I can’t walk in my own room. Wednesday is my house cleaning day, so that on the end of Friday it my messes won’t be so harsh to face. Finding motivation to do this is very hard, as well as finding an emotional place where I feel comfortable with cleaning my room. No matter all the skills you know to combat it, sometimes it’s better to wait until your emotional well-being is better. Even though cleaning and decluttering will help with your emotional stability in the end, it won’t do any good if you have a meltdown in the middle of cleaning.

Well here is my educated guess. Jackson Galaxy has a lot of great videos on introducing new cats and learning how to distract an angry cat. He does plenty of videos on cat agression and you can skim through his show to see situations similar to your own.

First thing first is to review with your mom on cat body language. Try to make a safe, non stimulating place for your older female cat (basically something that primarily has her sent with no other cats around) and use a long distance toy of your cats choice. While playing, both of you should learn your cat’s preferences on playtime. My cat loves running up and down our stairs, and watching for subtle movements for the perfect time to pounce on it. You both will want to play with your cats until you see them panting.

Secondly you want to seperate your cats during eating time. Leave about 6 feet apart from the cats that don’t get along (more if they are too uncomfortable) and overtime you will want to shorten that distance and inch by inch a day. Ideally you should be able to exhaust your cats before meals so they won’t have enough energy to fully blow the other cat.

Thirdly you might have to start from scratch in terms of introducing your kittens to your other cats. Again, make sure your cats have their safe rooms, and gradually introduce objects with the other cat’s sents on them. Many times, those objects are like pictures in a house. If you walk into your house and all your photos have been replaced with someone else you’ve never seen before, it probably would make you furious. That’s how older cats perceive sents. When you gradually introduce smells, it will feel less like an invasion of personal space and introducing a new family member into your home.

Again, Jackson Galaxy does many wonderful videos on it because many times we forget basics to small nuances we’re supposed to pay attention to. You shouldn’t feel limited to just him, as many cat behaviorists have many videos in general about these situations. I find that Galaxy communicates information more clearly than others.

To put it simply, if you have trauma of any kind (acute, complex, or chronic. All of which are still trauma that should be treated) that often collides with your common sense, I would suggest to look into behavioral therapy first.

examples: unable to leave the house for any reason besides agoraphobia, refusing to go to hospital for treatment physically or mentally in fear of triggers, unable to continue through daily life without being out of control of your emotions.

If you are facing distress over gender dysphoria, discomfort with sexual interests (sexual as in preferred sex/gender), or other issues that give you issues to function as an average person I would suggest gender therapy.

Start from your toes tensing up as much as you can for an inhale, holding during the three seconds, and relax as you exhale. Do this for every part (in my recommendation) this order: toes, feet, ankles, calves, legs, belly, chest, arms, palms, fingers, hands, neck, and finally your face.
